```{r}
#| label: setup
library( data.table )
d <- function( f ) fread( file.path( "data", f ), encoding = "UTF-8" )
src <- d( "sources.csv" ); man <- d( "frozen_manifest.csv" )
dict <- fread( "../docs/variable_dictionary.csv", encoding = "UTF-8" )
cites <- function( k ) vapply( strsplit( k, ";\\s*" ), function( x ) paste0( "[@", paste( x, collapse = "; @" ), "]" ), "" )
md <- function( x ) gsub( "\\$", "\\\\$", gsub( "\\|", "/", x ) )   # keep pipe tables intact; "$" is not math
```

The database is built from `r nrow( src )` sources. Every file the build reads is
frozen on Amazon S3 with a SHA-256 checksum, so the published tables can be rebuilt
exactly even after a publisher revises or removes a file: `r format( nrow( man ), big.mark = "," )`
files, `r sprintf( "%.1f", sum( man$bytes ) / 1e9 )` GB. Part 4 shows how to restore
them. Each source folder in [`inputs/`](https://github.com/lecy/multiverse/tree/main/inputs)
has a `SOURCE.md` with the publisher, URL, years, how the file is obtained, the build
steps that read it, the licence and the citation.

# Sources

**Why frozen** records the reason each source is archived rather than only downloaded
on demand:

- **archive needed:** not reliably available online. The file was placed by hand, is
  behind a login, was shared with us, or has no recorded download URL.
- **on demand (release):** a fixed public release that a script downloads. It is frozen
  as a safeguard.
- **on demand (moving):** a public file that the publisher revises in place, so a
  later download can differ.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sources
#| tbl-cap: "Data sources. Files and GB are the frozen copy on S3."
#| output: asis
t <- src[ , .( Source = sprintf( "**%s**<br>`%s` %s", md( title ), folder, cites( cite ) ),
               Years = md( years ),
               `Why frozen` = archive, Files = files, GB = sprintf( "%.2f", gb ) ) ]
cat( knitr::kable( t, format = "pipe" ), sep = "\n" )
```

## Licences and redistribution

Federal sources are public domain. NCCS data are under the Open Data Commons
Attribution License (ODC-BY 1.0), PatentsView under CC BY 4.0, the MEDSL election
returns under CC0 and the McGovern election files under the MIT License. Two sources
have no open licence: the Religious Congregations and Membership Study (ASARB) and the
NERCRD social capital index. We received permission to redistribute both, and each
frozen folder carries a `PERMISSION.md`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-licences
#| tbl-cap: "Licence of each source, as stated by the publisher."
#| output: asis
cat( knitr::kable( src[ , .( Folder = sprintf( "`%s`", folder ), Licence = md( licence ) ) ], format = "pipe" ), sep = "\n" )
```

# Frozen-file manifest

Frozen inputs live at `s3://lecy/nonprofit-density/inputs/<folder>/`. Each folder holds
the files, a `MANIFEST.csv` (path, bytes, SHA-256, original path, the build steps that
read the file, freeze date) and the `SOURCE.md`. The full list of files with checksums
is in [frozen_manifest.csv](data/frozen_manifest.csv).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-frozen
#| tbl-cap: "Frozen files by source folder."
#| output: asis
f <- man[ , .( Files = .N, MB = round( sum( bytes ) / 1e6, 1 ),
               `Read by steps` = paste( sort( unique( unlist( strsplit( steps[ nzchar( steps ) ], ";" ) ) ) ), collapse = ", " ) ),
          by = .( Folder = sprintf( "`%s`", folder ) ) ]
f <- rbind( f, data.table( Folder = "**Total**", Files = sum( f$Files ), MB = round( sum( f$MB ), 1 ), `Read by steps` = "" ) )
cat( knitr::kable( f, format = "pipe", format.args = list( big.mark = "," ) ), sep = "\n" )
```

`soi` and `nccs-bmf` (the unified BMF) were frozen before the others and keep their
own layout. `env/restore_inputs.R` handles both.

# Final tables

The build produces two analysis tables, one per geographic unit. Both are annual,
2000–2024.

| Table | Unit | Rows | Columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/analysis/county_year.parquet` | 3,144 counties (2023 delineation, Connecticut planning regions) | 78,600 | 354 |
| `data/analysis/cbsa_year.parquet` | 925 core-based statistical areas: 387 metropolitan, 538 micropolitan [@data_omb_cbsa] | 23,125 | 422 |

Covariates observed only in some years come in up to three versions: `_obs` (observed
values only), `_lin` (linear interpolation between observed years) and `_locf` (last
observation carried forward). The dictionary marks these with *gap-fill*.

# Variable dictionary

```{r}
#| label: dict
#| output: asis
dict[ , table := fifelse( table == "both", "county and CBSA", fifelse( table == "county", "county only", fifelse( table == "cbsa", "CBSA only", table ) ) ) ]
for ( g in unique( dict$group ) ) {
  x <- dict[ group == g ]
  cat( "\n## ", tools::toTitleCase( gsub( "_", " ", g ) ), " {.unnumbered}\n\n", sep = "" )
  cat( knitr::kable( x[ , .( Variable = sprintf( "`%s`", variable ), Description = md( description ),
                             Table = table, Step = step, `Gap-fill` = fifelse( gapfill, "yes", "" ) ) ],
                     format = "pipe" ), sep = "\n" )
}
```

The dictionary is generated from the build scripts by `docs/make_dictionary.R` and is
also available as [variable_dictionary.csv](https://github.com/lecy/multiverse/blob/main/docs/variable_dictionary.csv).

# Software

The build runs in R [@r_core] with package versions pinned by renv [@pkg_renv]. It uses
data.table [@pkg_datatable] and arrow [@pkg_arrow] for data handling and fixest
[@pkg_fixest] for the panel models. This site is built with Quarto [@quarto].
